title: Parameters, arguments, return values
learningObjectives: Explain parameters, arguments, return values and write reusable JavaScript functions or control flow.

understand.concept: Parameters are names listed in a function definition; arguments are the values supplied when the function is called. return ends the function and sends a value back to the caller. Without an explicit return, a function returns undefined.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear parameter names and return values make functions easier to reuse and test. Avoid relying on hidden global state when a function can receive its required data as parameters.
understand.analogy: Parameters are the labelled input slots in a recipe; arguments are the actual ingredients supplied; the return value is the result.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript execution, hoisting, and parameter evaluation follow language rules.

explain.narrative: completed and total are parameters; 6 and 10 are arguments; the function returns a formatted string.

examples.explanation: completed and total are parameters; 6 and 10 are arguments; the function returns a formatted string.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function or control-flow result described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a function that accepts a name and score and returns a summary string. Test it with different arguments.
practise.independentTask: Create a small program that uses the control structure or function concept. Test normal, boundary, and optional-input cases.
hints: Keep inputs explicit and return results where practical.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Parameters, arguments, return values</title></head><body>
<script>function formatProgress(completed,total){return `${completed} of ${total} lessons`; }const summary=formatProgress(6,10);console.log(summary);</script>
</body></html>

<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Parameters, arguments, return values</title></head><body>

questions.prompt: What does the return statement do?
options: Ends the function and sends a value back to the caller
questions.answer: Ends the function and sends a value back to the caller
questions.explanation: return exits the current function and provides its result to the caller.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reuse and test?
options: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
Hidden global state and unrelated side effects
A very long function with many unrelated tasks
questions.answer: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
questions.explanation: Focused functions with clear inputs and outputs are easier to reason about and test.
